## Build CLI using Termux

1. Install [Termux](https://termux.dev)
2. Install dependencies:
   ```sh
   pkg install cmake clang make
   ```
3. Clone the repository:
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
   ```
4. Build:
   ```sh
   cd llama.cpp
   cmake -B build -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF
   cmake --build build --config Release -j
   ```
5. Run:
   ```sh
   ./build/bin/llama-cli -m <model>
   ```

## Build CLI using Nix

1. Install [Nix](https://nixos.org/download)
2. Clone the repository:
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
   ```
3. Build:
   ```sh
   cd llama.cpp
   nix build .#llama-cpp
   ```
4. Run:
   ```sh
   nix run .#llama-cpp -- -m <model>
   ```

### CUDA 12.8+

CUDA 12.8+ requires CMake 3.25+ to build.

## MUSA

This provides GPU acceleration using a Moore Threads GPU. Make sure to have the [MUSA toolkit](https://developer.mthreads.com/) installed.

```bash
cmake -B build -DGGML_MUSA=ON
cmake --build build --config Release
```

## HIP

This provides GPU acceleration using an AMD GPU. Make sure to have the [ROCm](https://www.rocm.com/) toolkit installed.

```bash
cmake -B build -DGGML_HIP=ON
cmake --build build --config Release
```

### Non-Native Builds

By default llama.cpp will be built for the hardware that is connected to the system at that time.

## Verifying that the CPU is not throttling
If the CPU is throttling, then performance will suffer. This can happen if the CPU is overheating, or if the power supply is not providing enough power. You can check the CPU temperature with a tool like `htop` or `coretemp`. If the CPU is overheating, then you should improve the cooling of the CPU, or reduce the workload.
